rows.description: I prayed hard and my wish did not come true, and now I wonder whether anyone hears. Doubt is honest. I can talk to a trusted elder about it instead of hiding it or feeling wicked.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, gratitude, rejection, respect, trust, worship
related mind states: curiosity, doubt, awe, trust

rows.description: Diwali, Eid, Christmas or Baisakhi means sweets, new clothes and guests, and I am bubbling. Joy is good; a mature child also remembers those who cannot celebrate and shares a little.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, gratitude, rejection, respect, trust, worship

rows.description: At the gathering I am told I cannot join because of who I am. It hurts and confuses me. It is not my fault; I can tell a trusted adult and know that real faith does not shut a child out.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: acceptance, gratitude, respect, trust, worship
related mind states: confusion, trust, hurt

rows.description: My friend fasts, wears a cross, or eats different food, and I want to know why. Asking kindly and listening shows respect, and I learn that different ways can each be sincere.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: hurt, loyalty, mockery, prejudice, respect

rows.description: My friend invites me to his festival and explains each thing patiently. I feel welcome. I can join with respect, without needing to agree or feeling that my own faith is threatened.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, hurt, loyalty, mockery, prejudice

rows.description: I laugh at a classmate's prayers or clothes because others do. It feels like fitting in, but it hurts someone. Standing quietly aside or changing the subject is braver.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, hurt, loyalty, prejudice, respect

rows.description: Classmates mock my prayer or dress. I feel ashamed of who I am. There is nothing wrong with my faith; I can tell a teacher and lean on friends and family who love me.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, loyalty, mockery, prejudice, respect
related mind states: affection, shame, hurt

rows.description: An elder says people of that faith are bad. I feel confused because my friend seems good. I can hold on to my own experience and ask questions, without being rude to the elder.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, hurt, loyalty, mockery, respect

rows.description: When someone insults my friend's religion, I speak up even though it is uncomfortable. Friendship shows in defending someone's dignity, not in staying silent.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: curiosity, hurt, mockery, prejudice, respect

rows.description: I stand tall for the anthem and feel goosebumps on Republic Day. Pride in the country feels warm; a wise child also learns that love for one's land includes caring for all its people.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: awe, confusion, mockery, respect
